\chapter{Boolean Analysis — DNF}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.KKL.DNF
\section{Overview}
Bounded-width disjunctive normal forms have explicit Fourier tails and total influence bounds. These estimates yield Boolean junta approximations whose coordinate count is polynomial in reciprocal error for each fixed width.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier tail of a regular DNF]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.dnf_fourierWeightAbove_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, RestrictionFourier.odonnell_lemma_4_21, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p101-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p101-b005
}
\difficulty{6}
Let $d$ be a DNF on $n$ variables of width at most a positive integer $w$. Suppose every term has no repeated literals and any two literals in a term sharing a variable are equal. For every $t\in\mathbb N$, its sign encoding $f(x)=(-1)^{d(x)}$ satisfies $\sum_{|S|>120w(t+1)}\widehat f(S)^2\le8\,2^{-t}$ under the uniform cube law.
\end{theorem}

  {RestrictionFourier.odonnell_lemma_4_21}
  {context}

\proofstep
  {BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.dnf_fourierWeightAbove_le}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p100-b005,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p101-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p101-b005}
\difficulty{1}
Let $d$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ Boolean variables, let $w,t\in\mathbb N$,
and suppose the width of $d$ is at most $w$ and $w>0$. For the real-valued function $f$
that equals $-1$ where $d$ evaluates to true and $1$ where it evaluates to false, the
Fourier weight on levels strictly above $120w(t+1)$ satisfies
$\sum_{|S|>120w(t+1)}\widehat f(S)^2\le 8(1/2)^t$, with Fourier coefficients and
expectation taken under the uniform cube measure.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
Let $d$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ satisfy
$d(x)=1$. The number of coordinates whose individual flip changes the sign encoding of
the formula's value is at most the maximum width of a term of $d$, taken to be $0$ if
$d$ has no terms.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[DNF total influence bound]

\difficulty{5}
For every DNF formula $d$ on $n$ Boolean variables, the total influence under the
uniform measure of the sign encoding of its value is at most twice the width of $d$,
where the width is the maximum term width and is $0$ for an empty formula.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Parameters for DNF approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.dnf_junta_parameters}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that for every positive integer $w$ and every real number
$\epsilon$ with $0<\epsilon\le 1/2$, there is a natural number $t$ for which
$8(1/2)^t\le\epsilon$ and $\frac{(2w)^3}{\epsilon^2}9^{120w(t+1)}\le(1/\epsilon)^{Cw}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Junta Approximation for DNF]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.dnf_junta}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeVariance_eq_sum_nonempty_fourier, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.dnf_fourierWeightAbove_le_of_width, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.dnf_junta_parameters, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.dnf_totalInfluence_le_two_mul_width, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.exists_boolean_constant_approximation, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.friedgut_junta, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowInfluence_fourierConcentration, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsClose, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.disagreementProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, BooleanAnalysis.parseval_pm_one, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence, BooleanAnalysis.totalInfluence_eq_sum_sq_deg, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, KKL.IsJunta, KKL.influentialCoords}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p269-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p269-b006
}
\difficulty{5}
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that for every $n,w\in\mathbb N$ and every DNF $d$ on
$n$ variables with width at most $w$, and every $0<\varepsilon\le1$, there are a
coordinate set $J\subseteq[n]$ and a function $h:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on
coordinates in $J$ such that $|J|\le(1/\varepsilon)^{Cw}$ and the uniform probability
that $h(x)$ differs from the sign encoding of $d(x)$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}
